claims: the EVM's execution model: a stack machine with 256-bit words, metered operations, and storage, memory and calldata as distinct spaces
its call model: message calls, delegate calls and the context they carry
the consequences of its design for programs: expensive storage, bounded call depth and control passing to external code
WASM as a portable instruction format: a typed stack machine with structured control flow, validated before it runs
what a blockchain must constrain to run WASM deterministically: floating point, memory growth, metering and host functions
the languages and toolchains WASM opens to on-chain programs
what makes a virtual machine provable: execution recorded as a trace that a proof system checks against constraints
instruction-set choices that keep proving cheap: RISC-style or custom instructions and field-friendly arithmetic
the costs of a zkVM: prover time and memory against verification cost, with zero knowledge optional
